steps.text: It all started in the company bathroom. That day, I was sobbing uncontrollably on the toilet, overwhelmed by despair over my chaotic life.

Outside the stall, a few colleagues who had just returned from a trip to Sargon were chatting about their vacation. From their conversation, I overheard a name and a profound theory that helped me calm down.
And so I packed my bags and traveled from the steel jungles of Columbia to the dense rainforests of Sargon, braving countless hardships along the way. Eventually, I arrived here and met the sage.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Welcome to the Sanctuary. So, did you meet the sage today?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: I did. It was truly an honor. Even though it was quite late, he still listened patiently to my questions and shared his wisdom.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: What did he say?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Nothing. He just coiled the rope in his hands, without saying a word.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: ...Rope?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Yes. He was trying to show me my troubles were like tangled threads: if I just have enough patience, I can untangle them to be weaved into sturdy ropes.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: And those ropes will rest neatly in my palm. They will no longer cause me any headaches.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: That... makes sense. The sage is as wise as ever.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Of course, you're also very perceptive, to be able to grasp the sage's wisdom so quickly.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Yes. Before I left, he gave me a long, contemplative look. I think he was praising me, in his own way.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Yes. I think you're right.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: To be honest, at first I thought this whole 'spiritual journey' thing was all just a rumor.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: No. We follow the sage. He has never led us astray.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: I think I'll sleep soundly tonight.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Then go sleep. Tomorrow's sermon will start at 8:00 A.M. sharp. I will be there to escort you all to the lecture hall.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: ...Each person walks through their life alone.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Like a solitary boat drifting on a lake...
The sage sits cross-legged on a massive rock in the lake beneath the waterfall, calmly sharing insights gained from observing the flowing water with the crowd gathered on the shore.
The crowd listens intently, letting his gentle words seep into their hearts.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Hello, friend. When did you arrive?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Just yesterday. How about you? How long have you been here?

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Almost a month now. Hard to believe, right? Just a month ago, I was still stuck in the shadow of my last relationship, completely dejected.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: But you look positively enlightened... Oh, I get it. It's because of the sage.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Yes. He led me out of the pain and darkness.
Hearing the chatter from the crowd, the sage pauses for a moment, gazes into the distance, and smiles warmly at everyone.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Shh. The sage is looking my way! I...

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: The sage's gaze is so warm. All my pain and suffering just melt away under it.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: As I look into his eyes, so full of compassion, understanding, and detachment, I can finally find harmony with everything around me.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Everything that happens to us is but like flowing water...

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: All will flow away, and all will pass.

steps.name: Bolívarian Traveler
steps.text: Look! He's reaching out towards us. That's his signature move!

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Shh! He's gonna say it! This is my favorite part!

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Say what? What's the sage going to say?

steps.name: Leithanan Traveler
steps.text: Just wait a minute, and you'll find out.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Ask nothing from life...

steps.name: All Travelers
steps.text: Let the river take me where it will!

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Wooooah.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Totter, you stopped in the middle for a little bit. Why?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: I heard someone's voice in the crowd, so I stopped to take a look.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Oh? Who was it? Which of them weren't paying attention?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: I don't know. I wasn't wearing my glasses, so I couldn't see.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Tch... Can we find a new location for the next sermon? There are too many mosquitoes here by the water.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Ahem, there won't be a next one. According to our script, you're about to step out of the spotlight.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: About time...

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Thanks to you, we've made a fortune off of these tourists over the past few months.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: *sigh* If only we hadn't been dead broke these past few years, we wouldn't have bothered a sick person like you.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: It's fine. Being away from my hometown for so long and coming back empty-handed... I have to admit, I do feel a little guilty. So I'm glad I can help.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: After all, it was the villagers who pooled the money for my travel expenses after my father passed. Now it's my turn to repay their kindness.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: I must admit, I feel a bit embarrassed for disturbing the peaceful final chapter of your life.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: I didn't expect saving that tour group would bring so much trouble. No idea what they said when they got back that brought all these people here...

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: At first, I thought someone important had come to the village.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: When I listened to their story, I realized they were looking for you. Back then I just wanted to play along and make a little in the process.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: So, you were already planning to rip them off?

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: I just told them what they wanted to hear. It takes effort and skill to speak to people's emotions. So what if I charge them a little for it?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: (Narrows eyes)

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Compared to those psychiatrists in the nomadic cities, it's practically pocket change.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Why did you return the money I gave you, anyway? It was quite a lot. There's really nothing you want to buy?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Not a thing. I just want to live out the rest of my days in peace and tranquility.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: As long as you embrace the flowing river, you will find your way to the distant horizon.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: ...Isn't that from tomorrow's script?

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Ha. Seems like you've already memorized your lines.
My time working together with the sage was indeed short.
After spending half a month in the rainforest, he suddenly announced to everyone that he was leaving to embark on a new journey to somewhere entirely new.
He announced his own death.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Hello, sir. Has there been an emergency?

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: I'm just as clueless as you are. All I know is the sage told me to gather everyone here.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: What? Why didn't you tell us earlier? I'm still in my pajamas. I can't go see him wearing this.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Worry not, for the sage does not care about such trivial matters.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Good. Oh look...
A few hornbeasts slowly walk out of the rainforest, stopping by the waterfall. A few seconds later, more animals walk out, settling at the riverbank.
A fin leaps out of the water, but the ripples it creates do not disappear.
Immediately, everyone realizes that the river and the waterfall are frozen in place. In fact, they stopped flowing some time ago.
The sage slowly makes his way out from behind the curtain of water, clad in plain clothing.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Fellow travelers. I am sorry to keep you waiting.
As soon as he starts speaking, the river starts flowing again.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: The sage!!!

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Hey! Hey! Stop shoving your way to the front!

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: I have to get closer to him, so he can see how much I support him!

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Sage, the sun has only just risen. What do you wish to tell us?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Last night, while exploring the jungle, I saw starlight filtering through the gaps in the leaves, falling onto the surface of the lake, and I...

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: *sigh*... Fellow travelers...

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: It was there I saw that my days are nearing their end. I called you all here today, to bid you farewell.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Surely you're joking, dear sage?

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Nonsense. The sage never tells jokes!

steps.name: Bolívarian Traveler
steps.text: Sage, does this mean you can see your own future?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: The past and the future are just two segments of the same river. As long as we are in the river, we can decipher the messages from the future that come with those ripples.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: But glimpsing into one's own destiny comes at a price. I can feel this place rejecting me; my journey in this world is nearing its end.

steps.name: Victorian Traveler
steps.text: Sage, how can you be so indifferent in the face of death?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: I accepted my fate long ago. I have found my inner peace.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Fellow travelers, do not weep for me. For me, death is but the start of a new journey.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Wow. I see the tranquility in your face. It's clear as day...

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: I have long come to terms with everything I've experienced, just as the river embraces everything that flows into it and continues its journey toward the distant horizon.

steps.name: Bolívarian Traveler
steps.text: Sage, before you leave us, can you tell us how to interpret all of this?

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: It is not my place to reveal those hidden secrets.

steps.name: 'The Sage'
steps.text: Farewell, fellow travelers...
A fowlbeast lands on the sage's shoulder. He closes his eyes and lowers his chin, as if in some kind of trance.
The current surges beneath his feet, creating a whirlpool.
The water splashes violently. In the blink of an eye, the sage disappears into the vortex.
Only a small whirlpool is left, quietly spinning on the surface of the water.
In Columbia, I was a failure. I was dead broke, and my family was on the verge of breaking up. But this trip has given me the courage to face life again.
The sage's calm acceptance of his own fate has convinced me that there will always be a river to carry away the pain I've endured.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Odd... this isn't where we agreed on.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Can't trust the guy to dig a proper escape ditch.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Sage?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The river flows.... as the sands of time...

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Enough. I already know what's going on here.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You won't tell anyone, will you?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Did you know? I happen to be a Sarkaz mercenary.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Uhh... Relax, If I wanted to tell anyone, I would've done so a long time ago.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: From the very first day I arrived, I sensed something was off—simplistic platitudes like that rarely resonate with anyone.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: But I never saw anyone complain.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Why would we?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: The scenery is beautiful, the food is excellent, and to be honest, you looked quite striking in your 'Sage' getup.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Most important of all, the cost of living here is pretty reasonable. For us, it was the perfect place to spend a vacation.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: But every time I spoke, you guys all seemed so invested in what I was saying. Like, true believers.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Meh. I treated it as cosplay, or maybe dinner theater. I saw a similar performance in Lungmen once. Only that time, the guy was dressed up as a gangster.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I've never been to Lungmen.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: You should go some time. It's nice.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I don't think I'll get the chance.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Don't worry. No one's going to call you out.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Everyone comes here for a brief respite, a temporary escape from the troubles of real life. Who cares about the truth?

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: In the end, we will all return to our own rivers.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Just as the sage says.

steps.name: Columbian Traveler
steps.text: Yeah, just as the sage says. Our thoughts and troubles remain in our respective rivers.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Totter, you know... if you want to stay at the office, you can. Rhodes Island has a great hospice program.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Thanks, but I'd rather live out my days back in my hometown.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: But didn't you say you couldn't contact your family?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yeah, because they're all dead.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Then you want to return home to live alone?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Yup. Great, isn't it?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Great how?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: It's peaceful alone.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Having other people around pitying me would only be a pain.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Here, some dry clothes. Put them on.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: What took you so long?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...It's quite a ways from the waterfall to here. You couldn't find me a shortcut?

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Our other plan was to have you disappear in a flock of fowlbeasts. The problem with that one was you'd end up covered in poop.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Okay, you made the right choice.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I just hope that once I'm gone, my 'grand finale' will be enough to keep drawing a steady stream of tourists.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: To be honest, the rainforest is huge. There must be somewhere you can stay and rest. You don't need to leave.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: I promise that future visitors will not disturb your peace. We'll also pay for your food and clothing. If you need anything, just say the word.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No. I still plan on leaving.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Maybe everyone else sees me as a slick talker, but we grew up together—you know I wouldn't lie to you.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I know. I'm not stupid.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: ...Then why?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The sage is right. I should find my own river, the tranquil river that will embrace me and carry me onward.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Aren't you the sage?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No. I was just pretending to be him.

steps.name: Sage's Attendant
steps.text: Everything he said, I made it all up, Totter. It's all beastshit.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Doesn't matter. I've always gone with the flow anyway.
It doesn't matter whether the sage is 'real' or not.
What matters is that we all have our trials and tribulations. The day we accept that is the day we shall find true peace.
I think I'm ready to face my future again.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: It's been over six months since Totter returned to his hometown. In another six months, let's find some time to visit him together.
Hey... that's...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Totter?!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: ...Some stuff happened. Change of plans.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Anyway, I'm back now.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: So now you're planning to... uhh... I don't know what to think.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Oh good, now that you're back, I won't need to hunt you down in the rainforest. I've got a letter for you.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Huh? ...For me?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: From where?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: The snowfields.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: That's strange...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Field Operator
steps.text: Who sent it?

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Uhh... probably some old friends.
